summary: This best current practice describes how to reduce the harm from maintenance work by deliberately tearing down BGP sessions that will be affected, before the work begins. Traffic then shifts to other paths in a controlled way instead of being dropped when the link or device fails. It includes guidance for both ordinary IP networks and Internet Exchange Points.

eli5.summary: Before turning off a water pipe for repairs, you tell everyone to use a different tap first. Routers hang up on each other politely before maintenance, so nothing gets spilled.

subtitle: Hang up BGP sessions on purpose before maintenance, so traffic moves away while the network is still working.

tldr.problem: When a lower-layer network is taken down for maintenance, BGP sessions that cross it only notice the loss later, so end-user traffic is dropped while routers slowly converge.
tldr.mechanism: BGP Session Culling tears the affected sessions down before the work starts, either by the operator (Administrative Shutdown) or by the network's caretaker (a packet filter that blocks BGP), so traffic converges onto other paths while the forwarding plane still works.
tldr.outcome: Maintenance can then proceed with little or no traffic impact once traffic levels have dropped. This is a Best Current Practice and has not been obsoleted.

today: RFC 8327 is a Best Current Practice (BCP 214). The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it, so it remains the reference for this practice.

sections.title: What BGP Session Culling Is
sections.content:
BGP Session Culling is the practice of making sure BGP sessions are forcefully torn down before maintenance on a lower-layer network begins. Without it, the maintenance would cut the flow of data between the BGP speakers while their sessions are still up. With it, the speakers move onto alternative paths while the lower-layer network is still forwarding traffic normally.

The grace period needed is the time to detect the loss of the BGP session plus the time to converge onto alternative paths. The first is often governed by the BGP Hold Timer from RFC 4271, commonly between 90 and 180 seconds. The second depends on the implementation and could be as much as 15 minutes for a router with a slow control plane that receives a full set of Internet routes.

The RFC names two roles. The Caretaker controls the lower-layer network. The Operators administer the BGP speakers. Instead of a fixed grace period, both are encouraged to watch forwarding-plane activity and treat the culling as done once traffic has dropped to a minimum.
sections.eli5: If you are going to switch off a road for repairs, you first tell drivers to take another road. You wait until the road is quiet, then start digging.

sections.title: Voluntary Teardown by the Operator
sections.content:
In a voluntary teardown, the Operator issues an Administrative Shutdown on all BGP sessions that run across the lower-layer network, then waits a few minutes for data-plane traffic to subside. After the maintenance is finished, the Operator is expected to restore the sessions to their original administrative state.

A grace period is still needed. Architectures such as BGP Prefix Independent Convergence exist to speed up reconvergence, but an Operator cannot assume the remote side has them.

Initiators MAY use Graceful Shutdown (RFC 8326) to drain traffic smoothly before the session goes down. They MAY also use the Shutdown Communication (RFC 8203) to tell the remote side the nature and duration of the maintenance.
sections.eli5: Each network tells its neighbors, I am going away for a bit, so please use another route. Then it waits a few minutes before pulling the plug.

sections.title: Involuntary Teardown by the Caretaker
sections.content:
In an involuntary teardown, the Caretaker of the lower-layer network disrupts the BGP control-plane traffic itself. That makes the BGP Hold Timers of the affected sessions expire, which triggers rerouting of end-user traffic.

This matters most for a switched Layer 2 fabric such as an Internet Exchange Point (IXP). The RFC reports that operational experience shows many Operators cannot carry out the voluntary teardown, because of the cost and risk of coordinating the two configuration changes needed. That has an adverse effect on Internet performance.

So, when the lower layer gives no notification consistent with the planned work (for example, an Ethernet link down), the Caretaker of the fabric could choose to cull the BGP sessions on behalf of the connected Operators. This makes the Hold Timers expire ahead of the moment they would expire without intervention.
sections.eli5: If the neighbors will not hang up on their own, the person who runs the phone exchange quietly cuts the lines first, so everyone switches to another line before the real repair.

sections.title: Rules for the Packet Filter
sections.content:
The Caretaker culls sessions with a combined Layer 3 and Layer 4 packet filter in the switched fabric. The peering LAN prefixes used by the IXP form the control plane, and the filter design has these rules:

  • It MUST only affect BGP traffic specific to the Layer 2 fabric, not multihop BGP traffic that merely transits.
  • It MUST only affect BGP, which is TCP port 179.
  • It SHOULD allow for the bidirectional nature of BGP, since sessions may be established in either direction.
  • It MUST affect all Address Family Identifiers.
sections.eli5: The filter should block only the BGP phone calls between neighbors on that exchange, in both directions, and nothing else.

sections.title: Hardware Limits
sections.content:
Not all hardware can apply combined Layer 3/4 filters on Layer 2 ports. Even platforms that claim support may have limits or hardware resource failures when the filter is deployed, which can cause unexpected results. The RFC lists problems such as:

  • Layer 3/4 filters that cannot be applied on ports that already have Layer 2 filters.
  • Filters supported for IPv4 but not for IPv6.
  • Filters supported on physical ports but not on IEEE 802.1AX Link Aggregate ports, or the Caretaker failing to filter all such ports.
  • ACL hardware limits, fragmented ACL lookup memory, temporary service loss during hardware programming, and reduced ACL capacity if lossless ACL application is enabled.

The Caretaker is advised to know the limits of its hardware and to test complicated configurations in advance, so that problems do not appear during production deployments.
sections.eli5: Not every machine can do this trick. Try it on a test machine first so there are no surprises on the big day.

sections.title: Running the Maintenance
sections.content:
The Caretaker can watch data-plane traffic, for example interface counters, and carry out the maintenance with no traffic impact once the culling is complete.

The packet filters are recommended to be deployed only for the duration of the maintenance and removed immediately afterwards. To prevent unnecessary troubleshooting, Caretakers are RECOMMENDED to notify the affected Operators beforehand and say explicitly that involuntary BGP Session Culling will be applied.
sections.eli5: Watch the traffic until it has dried up, do the repair, then take the block away. And tell everyone ahead of time so nobody panics.

sections.title: Security and IANA
sections.content:
The Security Considerations section of the RFC states only that there are no security considerations. The IANA Considerations section states that the document has no actions for IANA.

The technique itself is operational. It drops BGP packets on purpose for a limited time, so the RFC's advice to tell affected Operators in advance is what keeps it from being mistaken for a fault.
sections.eli5: The authors say there is nothing risky to worry about here, and no new numbers to register.

sections.title: Example Packet Filters
sections.content:
The appendix gives example filters for an IXP whose control plane uses the peering LAN prefixes 192.0.2.0/24 and 2001:db8:2::/64. One example is for Cisco IOS, IOS XR and Arista EOS, the other for Nokia SR OS. Each denies TCP traffic between addresses in the peering LAN prefix on the BGP port in both directions, permits everything else, and is applied inbound on the port of the affected participant.

The RFC also points to a repository of configuration examples for other platforms.
sections.eli5: The back of the document shows the actual settings to type in, for a few popular brands of router.

Control-plane traffic is disrupted so the BGP Hold Timers expire

data.title: Cisco IOS, IOS XR, and Arista EOS (IPv4 part)
data.code:
ip access-list acl-ipv4-permit-all-except-bgp
   10 deny tcp 192.0.2.0/24 eq bgp 192.0.2.0/24
   20 deny tcp 192.0.2.0/24 192.0.2.0/24 eq bgp
   30 permit ip any any
!
interface Ethernet33
   description IXP Participant Affected by Maintenance
   ip access-group acl-ipv4-permit-all-except-bgp in
